BEGINNER1. Why Separate Data from Logic?

Definition

Test Data Management (TDM) in Tosca externalises the data values a Test Case uses — usernames, order quantities, expected messages — into a data source outside the Test Case itself: an Excel workbook, a database query, or Tosca's dedicated TDM Server. This lets one Test Case definition run once per row of data, called a partition, each producing an independent result.

Real-world analogy: TDM is like a mail merge in a word processor. You write the letter template once (the Test Case), plug in a contacts spreadsheet (Excel TDM), and the software produces one personalised letter per contact row (partition). Change the contacts list — the letter template stays untouched.

The Problem Without TDM

Without externalised data, testing three different login scenarios (valid admin, valid regular user, invalid credentials) would require three near-duplicate Test Cases, each hard-coding its own values — tripling the maintenance surface for what is really one scenario shape.

BEGINNER2. Excel TDM: The Simplest Approach

The most common entry point into TDM is binding a Test Case to an Excel workbook, where each row supplies one full set of parameter values.

// Excel TDM binding
1. Create Excel file:
   | Username        | Password   | ExpectedMsg        |
   | alice@test.com  | pass123    | Welcome, Alice     |
   | bob@test.com    | pass456    | Welcome, Bob       |

2. Link in TCM:
   TestCase → Properties → TestData → Select Excel file
   Map column "Username" → {P:Username}
   Map column "Password" → {P:Password}

3. TOSCA creates one partition per row → runs TC twice
💡 Tip: Excel TDM is the easiest way for non-technical team members to contribute test data — a business analyst can add a new row to cover a new scenario without touching TCM at all, as long as the Test Case is already bound to that workbook.

BEGINNER3. Data Partitions and Results

Each row in the bound data source becomes a partition — effectively a full, independent instance of the Test Case's steps, executed with that row's values, and reported as its own pass/fail result.

// Excel: TestData_Login.xlsx
Row 1: Username=alice@test.com, Password=pass123, Role=Admin
Row 2: Username=bob@test.com,   Password=pass456, Role=User
Row 3: Username=invalid,        Password=wrong,   Role=None

// TCM maps rows → 3 partitions of TC001_Login
// Run produces 3 results:
Partition 1 (alice) → Passed
Partition 2 (bob)   → Passed
Partition 3 (invalid) → Failed (login rejected — expected)
Note on "expected failures": Partition 3 above is designed to test that invalid credentials are rejected. Its Verify step should assert the rejection message, so a "Failed" login attempt actually shows as a Passed partition (the assertion about rejection succeeded) — don't confuse "the login failed" with "the test failed."

INTERMEDIATE4. Database TDM

For larger or more dynamic data sets, Tosca can pull partitions directly from a SQL query against a live database, using a Tosca DB Module connection.

// Add DB connection in TCM → Modules → Tosca DB module
Connection: TestDB
  Driver:   MSSQL / Oracle / MySQL
  Server:   db.test.internal
  Database: TestEnv

// SQL query as data source
SELECT username, password, role
FROM test_users
WHERE env = 'QA' AND active = 1

// Result rows become partitions — same as Excel TDM
Aspect Excel TDM Database TDM
Best for Small, manually curated data sets Large, dynamic, or environment-synced data sets
Who maintains it Any team member with Excel access Requires DB access/query knowledge
Freshness Static until manually updated Always reflects live database state at run time

INTERMEDIATE5. Buffer-Based Data (Runtime Capture)

Not all test data is known ahead of time. Data generated by the application itself during a run — an order confirmation number, a generated invoice ID — is captured into a Buffer using an Output step, then referenced in later steps. This is a complementary data source to Excel/Database TDM, used for values that simply don't exist until the test creates them.

// Buffer-based TDM (capture from previous step)
Step 3: OrderID [Output]   → stored as {B:OrderID}
Step 7: ConfirmOrderID [Verify] = {B:OrderID}
💡 Tip: See the Steering guide for the full mechanics of Buffers, including arithmetic and conditional use. TDM handles data that exists before the run starts; Buffers handle data that is only known during the run.

ADVANCED6. The Tricentis TDM Server

For enterprise-scale test data needs — especially where multiple teams or parallel DEX agents might otherwise grab and corrupt the same test record — Tricentis offers a dedicated TDM Server product. It provisions, reserves, and resets test data across environments as a managed service, rather than relying on static Excel files or ad-hoc SQL queries.

Capability What It Solves
Reservation Prevents two parallel test runs from picking the same "available" test user/account and colliding
Provisioning Creates fresh, valid test records on demand rather than relying on a finite pre-seeded pool
Reset Returns modified test data to a known-good state after a run for reuse
When you need this: once you introduce Distributed Execution (DEX) with many agents running in parallel, static Excel-row data sources become a source of race conditions — two agents may pick the same "unused" customer record simultaneously. TDM Server-level reservation eliminates that class of flaky failure.

ADVANCED7. Data Masking and Provisioning

When test data is sourced from production-like databases, regulatory and privacy requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) typically forbid using real customer PII directly in non-production test environments. TDM Server-class solutions include data masking — replacing real names, emails, and identifiers with realistic but fictitious substitutes while preserving referential integrity and data shape (e.g. still-valid formatted card numbers, consistent name-to-email pairing).

// Conceptual masking transform
Original:  Name=Jane Doe, Email=jane.doe@realcompany.com, SSN=123-45-6789
Masked:    Name=Test User42, Email=test.user42@example.test, SSN=000-00-0042
// Referential integrity preserved: same masked record used consistently
// across all tables/tests referencing that customer

INTERMEDIATE8. Choosing the Right TDM Approach

Use Excel TDM when: 
- Data set is small (a handful to a few dozen rows)
- Non-technical team members maintain it
- Data rarely changes between runs
- You're just getting started with data-driving
Use Database/TDM Server when: 
- Data set is large or must reflect live state
- Multiple parallel DEX agents run against it
- Regulatory masking is required
- Data must be reserved/reset automatically

INTERMEDIATE9. Common Pitfalls

  • Hard-coded literals disguised as "temporary": a literal test value left in a Test Step "just for now" often survives for years, defeating the purpose of TDM entirely.
  • Shared mutable data without reservation: two parallel runs modifying the same Excel row's referenced account causes intermittent, hard-to-reproduce failures.
  • Stale expected values: an Excel column with a hard-coded "ExpectedMsg" that no longer matches the application after a legitimate UI text change causes false failures.
  • Using real PII in test data: pulling unmasked production data into lower environments creates compliance risk.

BEGINNER10. Best Practices

1. Start with Excel, Graduate to DB/TDM Server as You Scale

Don't over-engineer data management for a two-scenario proof of concept — but plan the migration path once DEX and parallel execution enter the picture.

2. Keep One Row = One Complete, Independent Scenario

// Good: each row is self-contained and meaningful on its own
| Username | Password | ExpectedResult      |
| valid1   | correct  | Login succeeds      |
| valid2   | wrong    | "Invalid password"  |
| locked1  | correct  | "Account locked"    |

3. Version-Control Your Excel Data Files

Store TDM Excel files alongside other project artifacts in source control so data changes are reviewable and reversible.

4. Mask Anything Derived from Production

Never copy raw production exports into test data sources without a masking pass.

5. Reserve Shared Records Before Scaling Parallel Runs

Before introducing DEX with multiple concurrent agents, confirm your data source has a reservation/locking mechanism, or restructure so each agent gets its own data slice.

📋 Quick Reference Summary

Concept Key Points
TDM Externalises test data from test logic so one Test Case can run many scenarios.
Excel TDM Simplest binding; one row = one partition; easy for non-technical maintenance.
Partition One full, independent run of a Test Case with one row's data; own pass/fail result.
Database TDM SQL query supplies partitions; reflects live data at run time.
Buffer-based data Captures runtime-generated values (order IDs) — complements static TDM sources.
TDM Server Enterprise service for provisioning, reserving, resetting, and masking test data.
